full_judgment:
2. Undisputed facts are that the property in question was sold in auction on 9.5.94 in the court premises in pursuance of Artha Rin Execution Case No. 2 of 1991. The properties were advertised in the daily newspaper and after seeing the advertisement, the open auction was held and this opposite party No. 1 offered taka three lakh and, as such, he was declared as the highest bidder of the auction sale of the property in question. On the same day, the opposite party No. 1 deposited Taka 75,000.00 as part payment of the consideration money as per terms of the auction. Then the opposite party No. 1 filed an application on 9.6.94 praying for time to deposit the remaining amount of Taka 2,25,000.00 and the court, in spite of objection of the decree-holder, granted time to the opposite party No. 1 till 30.6.94 for depositing the same. On 30.6.94 the opposite party No. 1 filed an application for returning the part payment of Taka 75,000.00 on the ground that though the word buildings was mentioned in the auction notice, the opposite party No. 1 found a semi-pucca construction, that is, pucca wall with tin shed which is not consistent with the terms of the tender notice. On 13.7.94 the decree-holder filed an application to the court for treating the opposite-party No. 1 auction purchaser as defaulter in view of the fact that he did not deposit the balance amount of the auction money within the statutory period. However both the applications of the auction purchaser-opposite party No. 1 and the decree holder were taken up for hearing on 16.8.94. After hearing the matter, the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat passed an order stating that though in the tender notice the land was shown as 3-1/4th decimals in actual measurement it was found as 3 decimals and instead of building, it was found that there was a pucca wall with tin shed which are not in accordance with the terms of the tender. Holding the above the learned Judge directed to return Taka 75,000.00 to the auction purchaser. In the same order the learned Judge rejected the application of the decree-holder dated 13.7.94 by which the decree holder prayed for treating the opposite party No. 1 as defaulter and for retender of the mortgaged property in auction. Being aggrieved by this order dated 16.8.94, the decree-holder as petitioner preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. Faruque Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1, submits that this auction was held by the decree holder in collusion with the judgment debtor inasmuch as the auction purchaser was not given an opportunity to inspect the property in question. Such an argument at this stage is absolutely irrelevant and without any basis at all, inasmuch as no such application was filed before the Executing Court. Since the impugned order dated 16.8.94 is beyond the provisions of Order XXI Rules 85 and 86 of the Code of Civil Procedure and since the auction purchaser did not raise any objection about the quantum of land in his application and since the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat had no legal authority to extend the time for depositing the balance amount of Taka 2,25,000.00 we are of the view that the impugned order suffers from legal infirmity and the learned Subordinate Judge has committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside.
